paths.note: Pass template=exasol-analytics and the server injects dash_server_exasol.py if you did not supply it, so skipping the scaffold costs you nothing. Add your queries/*.sql in the same call.
paths.use_when: The dashboard is designed: you have written app.py and know which SQL it runs.

paths.note: An exploration tool. Read SCHEMA_NOTES.md and the generated queries/business/*.sql for the column choices, then keep what is useful. If the app is already designed, most of the 12 files get deleted one app_delete_file call at a time - use app_create_from_files instead.
paths.use_when: The schema is unfamiliar and you want the server to pick columns, relationship hints and catalog-backed SQL for you.

paths.note: The overview and kpi-trend patterns emit demo SELECT … FROM DUAL stubs, not catalog-backed queries.
paths.use_when: You want one of the prebuilt patterns below as-is - analytics-hub or ops-monitor for real SQL.

choosing_a_creation_path.rule_of_thumb: Already designed the dashboard? app_create_from_files. Still discovering the schema? app_scaffold_from_schema, then keep what it taught you.

patterns.best_for: The default exasol-analytics scaffold: a multi-tab app with system health, query history, and a business analytics placeholder ready for schema-specific SQL.
patterns.name: analytics-hub

patterns.best_for: Demo-only KPI/detail layout. Use this when you want to look at the layout shape before binding real SQL — the generated `queries/summary.sql` and `queries/detail.sql` are `SELECT … FROM DUAL` stubs with hard-coded numbers, not catalog-backed queries. For a real dashboard, write it and call `app_create_from_files`; to have the server propose one from the catalog, call `app_scaffold_from_schema`.
patterns.name: overview

patterns.best_for: Demo-only KPI + trend + detail layout. Like `overview`, the generated `queries/*.sql` are `SELECT … FROM DUAL` stubs with hard-coded data. For a real trend dashboard, write it and call `app_create_from_files`; to have the server pick a date column from your schema and emit catalog-backed SQL, call `app_scaffold_from_schema`.
patterns.name: kpi-trend

patterns.best_for: Operational Exasol monitoring dashboards using metadata, session, usage, and SQL history queries.
patterns.name: ops-monitor

recommendation: Default to `app_create_from_files` with template=exasol-analytics. You supply app.py, dash-app.json and requirements.txt; the server injects `dash_server_exasol.py` for you, so the app lands as 4 files and every one of them is used. Reach for `app_scaffold_from_schema` when you do not yet know the data and want the server to introspect the catalog and propose a starting point - it emits 12 files, which is exactly right for exploring and mostly ceremony to delete once the dashboard is already designed. `app_create_exasol_dashboard {pattern: kpi-trend/overview}` ships demo `SELECT … FROM DUAL` stubs and is never a starting point for real data; use `analytics-hub` or `ops-monitor` when their prebuilt SQL is what you actually want.
summary: Built-in Exasol dashboard patterns for profile-bound hosted app scaffolds.

template_guide.exasol-analytics: Profile-bound analytical scaffold with SQL files, a runtime helper, and a multi-tab structure designed for live Exasol queries. Also the template to pass to app_create_from_files so your own files get the Exasol runtime helper injected.
template_guide.metric-cards: Generic starter app with static metric cards. Use it when you are not building around a live Exasol profile.
